tasks.title: about the project
tasks.task:
This is going to be a simple 3D game engine, a merge of Unreal Unity and Godot with some design principals belonging to one or the other and a melding of the Three. My style is simple PSX style horror games so this engine will be geared towords that. For now we will work in 'main' and focus on the very very basics, before moving into more strucutres sub systems via branches

Language Used should be C++

tasks.title: Recompile scripts in place
tasks.task:
Editing a script in the Script Editor recompiles it on every change. compile() currently does types_[name] = std::move(newClassInfo), which frees the old ClassInfo while the component-registry factory lambda and every already-attached ScriptComponent still point at it -> use-after-free / crash when the script is then added to an actor or Play is pressed.

Fix: recompile IN PLACE. Keep the same ClassInfo object (stable pointer); swap its decl, re-resolve the base, re-index functions. Live ScriptObjects whose class changed should drop their cached state so field initialisers re-run and do_async resume indices reset.

requirements.text: recompiling a script keeps its ClassInfo pointer stable
edit a script, add it to an actor, hit Play -> no crash
edit a script already attached to an actor, hit Play -> the new code runs
script objects re-run field initialisers after their class recompiles

tasks.title: variables
tasks.task:
here we will setup base system types used for all or most components, as well as some of the data they will use.

note, the syntax for a base class is uppercase first letter. 'ie Actor" returns the global type actor, its what you should set your variable as to use a Actor reference. Lowercase is for instance 'ie actor" which returns the actor. for instance.

Actor a = this.actor; would return the actor base of the type.

if the object has a component that inherits from actor you can get it with this.get_component(type_of(Actor)); which returns the actor (or whatever type you give it). Or
Actor a = this.actor;
Actor b = a.get_component(type_of(Actor));

in that case get_component is a function of Actor, which a is an instance of. type_of is a global function which is used to pass a type.

Arrays can take any type even in the same array, and can be accessed via array_name[index] which returns it.

tasks.title: functions
classes
tasks.task:
classes are the types that actually get implemented and added to auto complete. classes can inherit from other classes or be inherited from. they can also be set to static (meaning instances CANNOT be made of them, they can be called from anywhere, and the update,start always run even if not instanced on any actors. Also they CANNOT be instanced on an actor and only 1 instance runs ever)

they can also be abstract which means they cannot be instanced and MUST be overriden. Each class must have a unique name that doesnt start with a number but does start with an Uppercase letter.

tasks.title: expressions
tasks.task:
expressions are ways to compare values, or change them
1 + 2 is an expression that returns 3
x + y returns the sum of 2 variables
1 == 1 returns true
1 != 1 returns false
1 == 2 returns false

"text" + "text" returns 'texttext'

all types (except string and char) should have .str() functions that return it as a string

"text" + 1.str() would then return "text1"

tasks.title: Asset browser context menu
tasks.task:
Replace the buttons at the top of the Asset Browser with a right-click context menu whose actions are organised into sub-menus. Remove the Import Image / Import Model / Create Material buttons entirely. Use the shared ui::ContextMenu framework so this matches the rest of the app and can be reused for other panels later.

New Script creates assets/scripts/<Name>.cscript from a template (a class inheriting Actor with empty start / update(float delta) / physics_update(float delta)), compiles + registers it, and opens it in the Script Editor. Names are made unique.

tasks.title: Live component reload and registry cleanup
tasks.task:
Two loose ends from live editing:
1. Renaming a class inside a script leaves the old name in the Add Component menu forever (ComponentRegistry::add dedupes by name and never replaces / removes).
2. A ScriptComponent already on an actor keeps running the old code until it is removed and re-added.

Fix: when a class is renamed, drop the old registry entry (or rename it); when a class recompiles, invalidate the cached ScriptObject on every attached ScriptComponent so edits take effect in the same session.

requirements.text: renaming a class in the editor removes the stale component-menu entry
a ScriptComponent attached to an actor reflects code edits without being re-added
